From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Private hosting gap analysis & next steps

Hi Tara / Kevin — thanks again for a focused call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth from the discussion: 

Summary of the call (high level)
- Primary goal: run low-latency inference for patient-facing triage flows inside Clarity Health's VPC / private environment.
- Drivers: regulatory/data residency (must remain in US), procurement requiring isolated network (air-gap or outbound-only egress patterns), and FIPS-like key management for PHI encryption.
- Traffic profile: ~200 qps peak conversational traffic, median request latency target <=200ms (p50), token volume estimate ~45M tokens/month during pilot.

Key constraints you flagged
- No inbound connections to application hosts (egress-only connectivity via proxy/NAT)
- Logs/telemetry must remain within the VPC; no external logging endpoints allowed
- Third-party services limited to a tight allowlist; any public egress must be pre-authorized
- Required evidence: SOC 2 (latest report), KMS/HSM architecture, data retention/exfiltration controls

What Redwood can bring / immediate asks
1) We will produce a short "networking acceptance matrix" that maps required firewall rules, ports, and IP ranges for a Private/VPC deployment (will include fallbacks for a dedicated-hosted option).
2) We'll share a condensed SOC2/infosec checklist and our recommended KMS integration pattern (HSM-backed or customer-managed keys).
3) Propose technical deep-dive (60 minutes) to run through the diagram and NAT/egress flow with your infra team — suggested windows below.
4) Provide a preliminary sizing & pricing sketch for reserved capacity and an on-prem licensing option.

Proposed immediate next steps (owners + dates)
- Tara / Kevin: share the current network diagram (subnet, NAT, firewall) and list of allowed outbound destinations — target: EOD Thu 11/5. [Attachment: clarity_network_diagram_v1.pdf if available]
- Rishi: deliver networking acceptance matrix + hosting ask summary — target: 11/4 EOD. [Attachment: redwood-hosting-ask-summary.pdf]
- Marissa (technical lead): run the deep-dive and produce configuration checklist — schedule proposed below.
- Procurement: we'll draft an overview of term options (reserved vs dedicated vs private) and an early cost estimator for Clarity's pilot.

Let me know if I missed anything or if the owners below should be updated. I'll queue the two artifacts and propose times for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-hosting-ask-summary.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]

From: Tara Singh <tara@clarityhealth.com>

Thanks Rishi — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Network model: we only permit egress through our perimeter proxy (no inbound TCP sockets to application subnets). The model you're describing (egress-only requests to Redwood) should work if TLS is used and the outbound destinations are allowlisted.
- Data residency: must host in US-East (we cannot permit non-US regions for PHI).
- Telemetry: logs for debug traces must be routed to an internal S3 bucket (no third-party SaaS log ingestion). We can provide an S3 endpoint in the VPC.
- KMS: customer-managed keys preferred; we have HSM-backed keys in our KMS (please confirm handshake/rotation expectations).

I've attached our current high-level network diagram. It shows NATed subnets + transit gateway connections to our on-prem environment. The diagram should make the egress patterns clear.

[Attachment: clarity_network_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)]

Procurement note: we expect an RFP in Q1 2027. For the pilot we need a rough TCO estimate focused on reserved capacity vs private deployment. Can you include both upfront licensing and monthly operational cost assumptions?

I'll assign Kevin as the infra point-of-contact for the deep-dive and will send the diagram to him as well.

—Tara
Tara Singh
Head of IT, Clarity Health

Tara — thanks for the diagram and the clarifications. I've compiled a short action matrix and attached a narrow SOC2 checklist we typically surface during early qualification. Summary of the action matrix below (owners and deadlines):

Action matrix (short)
1) Network acceptance matrix (Rishi) — deliver by EOD 11/04 (will include required egress IPs, ports, and proposed VPC endpoint patterns).
2) SOC2 & KMS expectations (Rishi) — share checklist and a short note on how customer-managed KMS maps into our key exchange / rotation flow.
3) Technical deep-dive (Marissa & Neha) — proposed: Fri 11/06 10:00–11:00 PT; please confirm Kevin availability.
4) Procurement pricing sketch (Rishi + Sales Ops) — initial reserved vs private estimate by 11/10.
5) PoC scope doc (Marissa) — short scope for a 4-week pilot: isolation test, latency verification, and log retention validation — deliver by 11/12.

Quick answers to items you called out:
- Egress-only model: supported. We'll produce an egress IP list and a TLS-based outbound handshake pattern to avoid inbound sockets.
- S3-based telemetry: supported via VPC endpoint; we'll show how the runtime can drop logs to an internal S3 bucket without external ingestion.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) and can integrate with most KMS providers. We'll include a short diagram showing the envelope encryption handshake and rotation window (we need to confirm rotation policy with your security team).

Attachments: socs_checklist.xlsx (short), redwood-hosting-ask-summary.pdf (networking matrix draft).

Next actions for you: please confirm Kevin as infra POC and share any compliance windows or blackout dates for the deep-dive. Also confirm whether we should include your procurement rep on the next thread.

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.company.com/deals/CLAR-2026-005) and pre-read folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-pre-read).

Regards,
Rishi
